title: Project Hail Mary
subtitle: Andy Weir
description: A lone astronaut wakes up with no memory on a spacecraft millions of miles from Earth. As he pieces together what happened, he realizes he may be humanity's last hope against an extinction-level threat.

reviews.text: The most fun I've had reading a book in years. Absolutely unputdownable.
Rocky is the best character in any book ever written. Fight me.

title: Yesteryear
subtitle: Caro Claire Burke
description: A sweeping romantic story that moves across time, asking what it means to love someone across the distance of years and memory.

reviews.text: Quietly devastating. I finished it in one sitting.
Beautiful prose, slow burn done right.

title: The Seven Year Slip
subtitle: Ashley Poston
description: When Clover moves into her late aunt's apartment, she keeps slipping back in time seven years — and meeting a man she's starting to fall for, despite knowing he belongs to the past.

reviews.text: The concept is so original and the romance is so tender.
Poston writes grief and love so beautifully together.

title: Better Than the Movies
subtitle: Lynn Painter
description: Liz has always believed her love story will be just like the movies. When her dream guy moves back to town, she enlists her annoying next-door neighbor Wes to help her win him over — with predictably complicated results.

reviews.text: Every romcom trope executed to perfection.
So cute and funny. Read it in an afternoon.

title: Verity
subtitle: Colleen Hoover
description: Struggling writer Lowen Ashby is hired to complete the remaining books in a bestselling series. While staying at the author's home, she discovers a disturbing manuscript that reveals dark secrets about the family.

reviews.text: That ending has me questioning everything. CoHo is unhinged and I love her.
Read it in one night. Could not stop.

title: Heart the Lover
subtitle: Lily King
description: A luminous novel about desire, connection, and the complicated terrain of the heart — told with Lily King's signature precision and warmth.

reviews.text: Lily King never misses. This is her best yet.
Dense but worth every page.

title: Strange Buildings
subtitle: Uketsu
description: The second installment in the Strange Houses series — a collection of unsettling, puzzle-like mysteries presented through architectural diagrams and chilling narratives.

reviews.text: Such a unique format. The mystery element genuinely got me.
Creepy and clever. Perfect for one sitting.

title: Sunrise on the Reaping
subtitle: Suzanne Collins
description: Set 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games, this prequel follows Haymitch Abernathy as a young man entering the arena — and discovering the dark machinery behind the games.

reviews.text: Haymitch deserved this. Collins still has it.
Darker than the original trilogy. Absolutely gripping.

title: The Only One Left
subtitle: Riley Sager
description: A nurse caring for an elderly woman suspected of killing her family begins to uncover the truth through a typewriter — one letter at a time.

reviews.text: The typewriter device is genius. Couldn't put it down.
Sager delivers again. That twist!

title: The Correspondent
subtitle: Virginia Evans
description: A story told through letters across decades — about love, loss, and the words we never quite manage to say in time.

reviews.text: I cried. I highlighted everything. A masterpiece.
The letters format makes it so intimate and real.

title: King of Gluttony
subtitle: Ana Huang
description: The sixth book in the Kings of Sin series. A billionaire bound by his darkest vice meets the one woman who might be his undoing.

reviews.text: The chemistry is off the charts as always.
Not my fave of the series but still a fun read.

title: Strange Pictures
subtitle: Uketsu
description: A collection of eerie visual puzzles and mysteries — each photograph hides a horrifying secret. Can you spot it before it's revealed?

reviews.text: Read it with the lights on. Trust me.
Some of these got me so good. Delightfully creepy.

title: The Silent Patient
subtitle: Alex Michaelides
description: A famous painter shoots her husband five times and then never speaks another word. A criminal psychotherapist becomes obsessed with uncovering the truth behind her silence.

reviews.text: That ending destroyed me. Did not see it coming.
A near-perfect psychological thriller.

title: The Night We Met
subtitle: Abby Jimenez
description: The second book in the Say You'll Remember Me series — a second-chance romance about the night that changed everything and the years spent trying to find their way back.

reviews.text: Abby Jimenez writes the most real, human romances.
Warm, funny, and genuinely moving.

title: Tuesdays with Morrie
subtitle: Mitch Albom
description: Every Tuesday, Mitch Albom visits his former professor Morrie Schwartz, who is dying of ALS, and learns life's greatest lessons about love, work, community, family, and how to die.

reviews.text: I ugly cried. Everyone should read this.
Simple but profound. Morrie is unforgettable.

title: I Who Have Never Known Men
subtitle: Jacqueline Harpman
description: Forty women are imprisoned underground with no memory of why. The youngest among them has never known the world above. When they escape, they find a desolate earth and must confront what it means to be human.

reviews.text: Haunting and unlike anything I've ever read.
Bleak but beautiful. The ending wrecked me.

title: Yours Truly
subtitle: Abby Jimenez
description: Two rival doctors start an unlikely pen-pal friendship. When Dr. Briana Ortiz agrees to pretend to date her nemesis Dr. Jacob Maddox to help him out of a jam, feelings become very hard to fake.

reviews.text: Jacob Maddox is everything. I am not okay.
The letters in this book are so wholesome.

title: Remarkably Bright Creatures
subtitle: Shelby Van Pelt
description: A grieving woman works the night shift at an aquarium. A giant Pacific octopus named Marcellus becomes an unlikely narrator — and the key to solving a decades-old mystery.

reviews.text: Marcellus is the greatest character in modern fiction. I said what I said.
Warm, witty, and quietly devastating.

title: Dear Debbie
subtitle: Freida McFadden
description: A woman receives a letter addressed to someone named Debbie — and what begins as a simple mistake unravels into something far more sinister.

reviews.text: McFadden keeps delivering. This one is deliciously twisty.
Not her best but still a very solid read.

title: The Deal
subtitle: Elle Kennedy
description: Pre-med student Hannah agrees to tutor hockey player Garrett in exchange for his help making her crush jealous. But their fake arrangement starts to feel very, very real.

reviews.text: Garrett Graham is the blueprint for book boyfriends.
Classic new adult romance done right.

title: The Score
subtitle: Elle Kennedy
description: Hockey player Dean DiLaurentis has never had a problem getting girls — until he meets the one who genuinely doesn't care. Allie Hayes is focused on her career, not his charm.

reviews.text: Dean is insufferable and I am obsessed with him.
Probably the best in the Off-Campus series.

title: Atmosphere
subtitle: Taylor Jenkins Reid
description: From the author of Daisy Jones & The Six comes a sweeping new novel about ambition, sacrifice, and what it costs to reach the highest heights — literally.

reviews.text: TJR does it again. I was completely absorbed.
Her best since Daisy Jones. Stunning.

title: The Love Hypothesis
subtitle: Ali Hazelwood
description: To convince her friend that she's moved on, PhD student Olive Smith kisses the first man she sees — the notoriously cold Professor Adam Carlsen. One fake relationship later, nothing is going to plan.

reviews.text: STEM girls this is our book. Adam Carlsen forever.
The fake dating trope has never been more chaotic and I loved it.

title: The Mistake
subtitle: Elle Kennedy
description: Hockey player John Logan has always gone after what he wants — except Grace Ivers. When he finally gets his shot, he blows it. Now he has to convince her he's worth a second chance.

reviews.text: Logan deserved his book so much. Worth every page.
Not as strong as The Deal but still really enjoyable.

title: Strange Houses
subtitle: Uketsu
description: The first book in the Strange Houses series. Each chapter presents a house diagram and a chilling mystery — something is always wrong with the picture. Can you figure it out?

reviews.text: Unique concept, some puzzles are genuinely unsettling.
Fun to read with friends. Lots of 'wait WHAT' moments.

title: Funny Story
subtitle: Emily Henry
description: Daphne's fiancé left her for his childhood best friend. That best friend's ex, Miles, is now her roommate. Obviously the only solution is to pretend to date each other for revenge.

reviews.text: Breezy and warm and genuinely funny. Peak Emily Henry.
The perfect beach read. Miles is adorable.

title: Never Lie
subtitle: Freida McFadden
description: Snowed in at a remote cabin, Tricia discovers a box of tapes recorded by a patient who went missing from a psychiatric facility decades ago — and starts to uncover a terrifying truth.

reviews.text: The tapes device is so effective. Stayed up until 3am.
McFadden knows how to keep you guessing.

title: My Husband's Wife
subtitle: Alice Feeney
description: A woman begins to suspect her husband is not who he says he is — and that the life she's built may be built on lies.

reviews.text: Classic Feeney — twisty, dark, and compulsive.
The atmosphere is suffocating in the best way.

title: The Housemaid
subtitle: Freida McFadden
description: Millie accepts a job as a housemaid for the Winchester family. But something is very wrong in this house — and escape may not be possible.

reviews.text: The twist at the end is absolutely wild. Did not see it coming.
McFadden's best. Devoured it in a day.

title: Days at the Morisaki Bookshop
subtitle: Satoshi Yagisawa
description: After a painful heartbreak, Takako retreats to her uncle's small used bookshop in Tokyo. There, surrounded by books and quiet afternoons, she slowly begins to heal.

reviews.text: Gentle and cozy. Like a warm cup of tea in book form.
Made me want to visit Tokyo immediately.

title: Animal Farm
subtitle: George Orwell
description: A group of farm animals overthrow their human farmer, hoping to create a society where animals are equal and free. But slowly, the pigs begin to consolidate power — and equality becomes a lie.

reviews.text: All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others. Chilling.
Short, brutal, and as relevant as ever.

title: The Wedding People
subtitle: Alison Espach
description: A woman checks into a Rhode Island hotel intending to end her life — but accidentally ends up entangled with a wedding party. What follows is an unexpected story about choosing to stay.

reviews.text: Quietly brilliant. Funny and heartbreaking at the same time.
One of the most humane books I've read in years.

title: Picking Daisies on Sundays
subtitle: Liana Cincotti
description: A sweet, slow-burn romance set against the backdrop of a flower shop and Sunday mornings — about learning to open your heart when you've been hurt before.

reviews.text: So soft and tender. Exactly what I needed.
The pacing is perfect. Every small moment lands.

title: The Last Letter
subtitle: Rebecca Yarros
description: A soldier begins a correspondence with a woman back home — not knowing she's the sister of his best friend, or that falling for her will complicate everything.

reviews.text: I sobbed. Rebecca Yarros writes the most emotional romances.
The letters are so beautiful. Finished it in one sitting.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
subtitle: Oscar Wilde
description: A beautiful young man's portrait ages in his place while he pursues a life of hedonism and moral corruption. Wilde's only novel — a meditation on vanity, sin, and the soul.

reviews.text: Every sentence is quotable. Wilde was built different.
Dark, decadent, and absolutely gorgeous.

title: Beach Read
subtitle: Emily Henry
description: Two writers — a romance author with writer's block and a literary fiction writer who doesn't believe in happy endings — dare each other to write outside their comfort zones. And fall in love.

reviews.text: This is what started my Emily Henry obsession. No regrets.
Gus and January have incredible chemistry.

title: Say You'll Remember Me
subtitle: Abby Jimenez
description: A chance encounter between a woman trying to escape her past and a man running from his future leads to a connection neither of them planned for.

reviews.text: Abby always writes the most lovable leads.
A great start to the series. Sweet and heartfelt.

title: Yellowface
subtitle: R.F. Kuang
description: After her Chinese American friend dies in a freak accident, June steals her unpublished manuscript and publishes it as her own. A razor-sharp satire of the publishing industry, race, and cultural appropriation.

reviews.text: Uncomfortable in the best possible way. RF Kuang is fearless.
A must-read for anyone interested in publishing.

title: Fake Skating
subtitle: Lynn Painter
description: A fake relationship between two figure skaters forced to compete as a pair spirals into something neither of them bargained for — on and off the ice.

reviews.text: Lynn Painter's fake dating energy never misses.
The skating scenes are so vivid and the romance is delicious.

title: Babel
subtitle: R.F. Kuang
description: Set in 1830s Oxford, a young student from Canton joins a translation institute called Babel — the center of Britain's imperial power. A dark academia fantasy about language, colonialism, and resistance.

reviews.text: Dense, brilliant, and absolutely devastating. A landmark book.
Kuang writes with such fury and precision.

title: Fourth Wing
subtitle: Rebecca Yarros
description: Violet Sorrengail is sent to the riders' quadrant to bond with a dragon — despite being too fragile for it. But the most powerful dragon on campus has chosen her, and so has the most dangerous man.

reviews.text: Xaden Riorson has ruined me for all other book boyfriends.
The worldbuilding is incredible and the romance is chef's kiss.

title: White Nights
subtitle: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
description: A lonely dreamer wanders the streets of St. Petersburg and meets a young woman named Nastenka over four magical white nights. A tender, melancholy novella about love and longing.

reviews.text: Heartbreaking in the most beautiful way.
Short but it will stay with you forever.

title: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes
subtitle: Suzanne Collins
description: Before he was President Snow, he was just a boy trying to survive. This prequel follows a young Coriolanus Snow as he mentors a tribute from District 12 and discovers the darkness within himself.

reviews.text: Understanding Snow makes everything about the original trilogy darker.
Lucy Gray Baird deserved better and I will die on this hill.

title: Daisy Jones & The Six
subtitle: Taylor Jenkins Reid
description: Told in oral history format, this is the rise and fall of a legendary 1970s rock band — and the complicated love at the heart of it all.

reviews.text: I kept forgetting this wasn't a real band. That's how good it is.
Billy and Daisy broke my heart across 400 pages.

title: Katabasis
subtitle: R.F. Kuang
description: RF Kuang's latest novel descends into myth and obsession — a story about a writer who goes too far in pursuit of the perfect book, and what she loses along the way.

reviews.text: Divisive but I was completely gripped.
Not for everyone but undeniably ambitious.

title: Mockingjay
subtitle: Suzanne Collins
description: Katniss Everdeen becomes the symbol of a revolution she's not sure she believes in. The brutal, devastating conclusion to The Hunger Games trilogy.

reviews.text: The most realistic conclusion to a YA dystopia ever written.
Dark and painful but exactly how this story needed to end.

title: Nothing Like the Movies
subtitle: Lynn Painter
description: The sequel to Better Than the Movies. Wes and Liz are back — but college has changed everything, and what worked in high school might not be enough anymore.

reviews.text: These two idiots in love. I missed them so much.
Doesn't quite hit the same as the first but still worth reading.

title: The Song of Achilles
subtitle: Madeline Miller
description: Patroclus, exiled prince and unlikely companion to the brilliant Achilles, grows up at his side and falls in love with him. A retelling of the Iliad told with devastating tenderness.

reviews.text: I sobbed for an hour. One of the greatest love stories ever told.
Miller writes Greek mythology like no one else.

title: The Alchemist
subtitle: Paulo Coelho
description: A shepherd boy travels from Spain to Egypt in search of treasure — and finds something far more valuable along the way. A timeless fable about following your dreams.

reviews.text: Changed how I see the world. A genuine classic.
Beautiful but a little on the nose. Still worth it.

title: Margo's Got Money Troubles
subtitle: Rufi Thorpe
description: Margo is broke, pregnant, and out of options. So she does the only logical thing — starts an OnlyFans with her washed-up pro wrestler father. A sharp, funny, surprisingly moving novel.

reviews.text: So funny and so human. Rufi Thorpe is wildly underrated.
The father-daughter dynamic is everything.
